title: VPC Airlift & Blue/Green Operator Handoff Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents the VPC Airlift deployment pattern and the operator-facing blue/green handoff sequence for Redwood Private customers. It is intended for field operators, SREs, and customer platform engineers responsible for commissioning, day-2 operations, and safe upgrade/rollback of private deployments where the control plane is partially hosted and the data plane runs inside a customer VPC or on-prem cluster.

Scope: Applies to VPC and hybrid private deployments that use:
- Redwood federated control plane (hosted) + tenant data-plane in customer VPC
- Operator-managed runtime (Kubernetes or equivalent container runtime)
- Tenant isolation and model artifact management via Redwood Agent and secure artifact registry

Key goals
- Provide a repeatable, low-risk blue/green cutover for model and runtime upgrades
- Define operator responsibilities for preflight, handoff, and rollback
- Document telemetry, SLOs, and acceptance criteria for safe promotion

Ownership and Contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments ops (oncall: #private-ops)
- Hand-off owner (customer): customer-platform-team (point-of-contact included in SOW)
- Escalation path: Redwood Field SE -> Private Deploy Eng -> Eng-SRE

Definitions
- Airlift pattern: control-plane components (auth, orchestration, orchestration APIs) hosted by Redwood; long-lived data-plane (runners, GPU workers, KV caches) deployed in customer VPC.
- Blue/Green operator handoff: method to stage an updated deployment (green) beside the active (blue) and flip traffic after acceptance checks.

Preflight checklist (operator)
1) Verify customer prerequisites
   - Network: customer BGP/route or VPC peering in place; RTT < 25ms to primary region (target for SLO-sensitive customers)
   - IAM/KMS: tenant service account created, KMS/HSM key available and accessible from data-plane nodes
   - Storage: NFS/S3-compatible endpoint reachable and meeting IOPS requirements
2) Control plane connectivity
   - Control-plane API reachable from data-plane: curl -sS https://controlplane.redwood.example/api/health (expect 200)
   - mTLS certificate exchange validated (cert expiry > 30 days)
3) Resource validation
   - GPU: required GPU types and counts present and tagged as rdp-tenant-<id>
   - Disk: model-store disk >= requested quota and with 99.9% availability SLAs in customer environment
4) Telemetry and RBAC
   - Metrics forwarder and log-shipping endpoints configured (prometheus remote_write, fluentd)
   - RBAC roles and operator accounts configured per template in Appendix A

Acceptance criteria (promotion from green -> blue)
- Functional: 100% of smoke prompts return syntactically valid responses within 10s for 95th percentile
- Performance: char-per-second generation throughput within 10% of baseline (baseline defined in tenant onboarding doc)
- Stability: <1% 5xx error rate across 15-minute window and no KV cache eviction regressions
- Telemetry: metrics and traces present for all model-serving pods; no missing spans for >5 minutes

SLOs and thresholds (example)
- Inference latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (≤64 tokens) under steady-state load (defined per tenant)
- Error budget: 0.5% monthly 5xx budget for control-plane RPCs
- Observability retention: last 7 days full-resolution telemetry in customer-forwarded metrics

Blue/Green operator handoff sequence (step-by-step)
1) Create green environment
   - Deploy new runtime version into green namespace (operator command):
     rdpctl deploy --tenant $TENANT --namespace green --manifest ./manifests/runtime-v2.yaml
   - Ensure image pulls are signed and verified: cosign verify --key $COSIGN_KEY new-image
2) Warm model cache and KV
   - Run model prefetch job: rdpctl prefetch --tenant $TENANT --models gpt-small,gpt-mid
   - Validate KV warm percentage > 90% after prefetch (see telemetry metric rdp.kv.warm_ratio)
3) Run acceptance suite (automated)
   - Trigger smoke & perf suite: rdpctl test --tenant $TENANT --suite handoff-smoke --output json > green-test.json
   - Verify test results: jq '.results | map(select(.status=="fail")) | length' green-test.json == 0
4) Canary traffic (optional; recommended for high-RTO tenants)
   - Route 5–10% of production traffic to green for 30 minutes: rdpctl traffic --tenant $TENANT --from blue --to green --percent 10 --duration 30m
   - Monitor p95 and error-rate dashboards during canary window
5) Promote to active
   - If no regressions after canary, perform final promotion: rdpctl promote --tenant $TENANT --target green
   - Confirm promotion via control plane: curl -sS https://controlplane.redwood.example/api/tenants/$TENANT/active (expect "green")

Rollback and safety windows
- Fast rollback: If error-rate > 2% or p95 > baseline + 50% within 10 minutes, execute immediate rollback: rdpctl rollback --tenant $TENANT --to blue
- For stateful changes (KV schema, model format): enforce a 48-hour safety window where rollback requires operator approval and a coordinated snapshot restore.
- Evidence capture during rollback: collect pod logs, model fetch traces, and KV snapshot(s) to an evidence bundle stored in customer S3 under s3://redwood-evidence/$TENANT/${TIMESTAMP}

Day-2 operational run actions
- Routine: weekly artifact integrity scan, daily node health checks, hourly pod restart rate alerts (threshold: >2 restarts per pod per hour)
- Capacity: enforce autoscaler floor defined in SOW; alert when queued request depth > configured burst threshold for > 10 minutes
- Drift detection: run config-diff cron every 6 hours and alert on unapproved changes to kube manifests or operator flags

Operational playbook (incident triage)
1) Detection: alert fires (p95 or 5xx) -> oncall acknowledges in 5 minutes
2) Initial triage (10 min)
   - Check control plane connectivity and last successful heartbeat (rdpctl heartbeat $TENANT)
   - Identify whether issue is control-plane, data-plane, or network
3) Containment (15–30 min)
   - If data-plane unhealthy, divert traffic to blue or Hosted fallback: rdpctl fallback --tenant $TENANT --policy hosted-failover
   - If control-plane degraded, scale up control-plane read replicas or enable degraded-mode API with reduced features
4) Remediation and postmortem: create incident in tracker, collect evidence bundle, and run post-incident regression tests before re-promotion

Configuration templates (examples)
- Kubernetes deployment settings (snippet, values.yaml style):
  replicas: "2"
  resources: |
    cpu: \"8\"
    memory: "32Gi"
    gpu: "1 nvidia-a100"
  livenessProbe: |
    exec: [\"/usr/local/bin/healthcheck\"]
    initialDelaySeconds: "30"
    periodSeconds: "15"

- Operator RBAC template (appendix A):
  ServiceAccount: rdp-operator-<tenant>
  Roles: ["rdp.operator.manage", "rdp.telemetry.push"]

Customer requirements matrix (table; operators must confirm)
- Network: "BGP or VPC peering configured; TLS termination allowed for egress; NACLs permit control-plane CIDRs"
- KMS/HSM: "AES-256 GCM capable; HSM silhouette supported; cross-account key grants configured"
- Storage: "S3-compatible endpoint with eventual consistency window < 5s; 5000 IOPS recommended for model-store"
- GPUs: "Driver version >= 525.x; CUDA 12.x; MIG profiles approved if using multi-instance GPUs"
- Compliance: "Audit logs exported to customer SIEM; retention policy >= 90 days for audit trails"

Troubleshooting matrix (common symptoms -> quick checks)
- Symptom: high cold-start latency
  Quick checks: model cache warm ratio, network egress RTT, storage throughput on model shards
- Symptom: KV inconsistency after cutover
  Quick checks: KV schema mismatch, read-after-write propagation delay, snapshot compatibility
- Symptom: Pod OOMs after upgrade
  Quick checks: resource limits changed, new runtime memory profile, library version mismatch

Appendix A — RBAC and service account examples
- Minimal operator role (YAML snippet):
  apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
  kind: Role
  metadata:
    name: rdp-operator-role
  rules:
  - apiGroups: ["rdp.redwood.io"]
    resources: ["deployments", "jobs"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "patch", "delete"]

Appendix B — Useful rdpctl commands
- deploy: rdpctl deploy --tenant $TENANT --manifest <manifest.yaml> --namespace green
- prefetch: rdpctl prefetch --tenant $TENANT --models <comma-separated>
- test: rdpctl test --tenant $TENANT --suite <suite-name>
- promote: rdpctl promote --tenant $TENANT --target <color>
- rollback: rdpctl rollback --tenant $TENANT --to <previous-color>
